items.title: 66100_Bud Freeman oral history interview
items.q: Dave Tough came over to see his girlfriend... especially Kenny Clark, Dave Tough came over to see his girlfriend

ctx.x: Well, of course, it was not until I was about 15 that I was to meet at Austin High School, I was to meet the McPartland brothers, Jimmy who is still going very strong, of course, married to Marian Mary McPartland, who is by the way coming over here to England and had a marvelous musical career. I saw Jimmy at Nice last year and he was just as good as ever and in wonderful condition.

Well, anyway, it was through Jimmy's effort that (You know,) I got a saxophone because he went to my dad and he said, I think Bud, he sings and he dances and I think he might have a natural talent for playing and why don't you consider buying him a C-Melody saxophone. That was the instrument one started on, I was not to continue that. We didn't know whether I could really get into playing, so now in the meantime before any of this happened Dave Tough, the great drummer, later to become I thought the best, with…

items.title: 66100_Bud Freeman oral history interview
items.q: Dave and Kenny Clarke Tough, Benny Carter and a few people like that who were later to become --

ctx.x: For the first time. There was no one -- of course, there was the great Bix and here unfortunately we did not -- the kids, and the young people listen to Bix today and even many musicians listen to Bix today,

and it is difficult to listen to Bix through all the other players because those players were not essentially jazzmen. They were men in the Whiteman band and in the Goldkette band who could read anything. They were fine disciplined musicians, but Bix out of a sense of loyalty, you know, playing with the men in the band used them on his records. They were not really, and I hope I am not being unfair when I say this, that they were not really jazzmen who lived the jazz music as did Louis and King and Bix and many…

I think that we then, as I said, never went back or as I meant to say, we never went back to the New Orleans Rhythm Kings, after hearing the King Oliver Band, because we realized that in hearing the King Oliver Band, we were listening to the real thing.
